author: J. A. Pack
title: Tennessee State Veterans Home Cleveland ranked 3rd among Bradley County nursing homes in Q1
text:
Tennessee State Veterans Home Cleveland was identified as the third largest nursing facility in Bradley County in the first quarter of 2026, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) reported .
The facility was equipped with 108 beds—33 fewer than the county average in early 2026—and served an average of 104 residents per day during the period.
CMS awarded Tennessee State Veterans Home Cleveland a 5 out of 5 overall rating, above the state average rating of 3 among Tennessee nursing homes.
For the quarter, Bradley Health Care & Rehab was the county’s largest nursing home, offering 213 beds. The next largest, Life Care Center of Cleveland, maintained 142 beds.
As of the first quarter of 2026, Tennessee State Veterans Home Cleveland reported no fines or penalties.
There was just one public nursing home in Bradley County, Tennessee, during this timeframe.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the older adult population in the United States is growing, while numbers in younger age groups continue to fall. Between 2020 and 2024, the number of residents 65 and older rose by 13%, as the under-18 population declined by 1.7%. Over the last century, older adults in the U.S. increased from 4.9 million in 1920 to beyond 61 million in 2024.
A 2021 report estimates nearly half of adults in this age range—about 28 million people—may require long-term services and support. The same study notes over a third will likely need care from nursing home facilities.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
